chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from 'Abdullah ibn Muskhan from al-Halabi from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the male slave, what is permissible for him from women? He said: 'Two free women or four slave women.'
ai.seo_question: How many women can a male slave marry according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the marital capacity of a male slave (mamluk), permitting him to marry either two free women or four slave women. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh where the status of the wife (free vs. slave) directly influences the number of permissible spouses, distinct from the general rule for free men. It underscores the flexibility in Islamic family law regarding social hierarchy and economic constraints.
